entries.title: Show the current folder
entries.explain: Prints the folder your session is working in.

entries.title: Go to another folder
entries.explain: Changes the working folder. Relative and absolute paths both work.

params.name: -LiteralPath
params.text: Treat the path exactly as typed, no wildcards

entries.title: Go to your home folder
entries.explain: The tilde stands for your user profile folder.

entries.title: Go up one folder
entries.explain: Moves to the parent of the current folder.

entries.title: Jump to a folder and come back
entries.explain: Push-Location remembers where you were, Pop-Location returns there.

entries.title: See the remembered folders
entries.explain: Lists the folders saved by Push-Location.

entries.title: List drives
entries.explain: Shows every drive letter with used and free space in bytes.

entries.title: Switch to another drive
entries.explain: Type the drive letter and a colon, or use Set-Location with the full path.

entries.title: Get the full path of a relative path
entries.explain: Turns a short path into the complete path and fails when it does not exist.

entries.title: Split a path into parts
entries.explain: -Leaf gives the file name, -Parent the folder, -Qualifier the drive.

entries.title: Build a path without worrying about slashes
entries.explain: Joins path pieces with the right separator.

entries.title: Find Desktop, Documents, Downloads
entries.explain: Works even when folders are redirected to OneDrive. Other names: MyDocuments, ApplicationData, LocalApplicationData, UserProfile.

entries.title: Check whether a file or folder exists
entries.explain: Returns True or False. Add -PathType Leaf for files or Container for folders.

entries.title: Open this folder in Explorer
entries.explain: Opens the folder in a new Explorer window.

entries.title: Handle paths longer than 260 characters
entries.explain: The \\?\ prefix lets Windows PowerShell 5.1 pass long paths to the file system.

entries.title: List files and folders here
entries.explain: Lists the content of the current folder.

entries.title: List everything below a folder
entries.explain: Lists files and folders in this folder and all subfolders.

entries.title: Show hidden and system files
entries.explain: -Force includes hidden and system items that Explorer normally hides.

entries.title: List only folders
entries.explain: Skips files. Use -File for the opposite.

entries.title: List files with one extension
entries.explain: -Filter is the fast way to match a pattern. Use -Include for several patterns together with -Recurse.

entries.title: Find the 20 largest files
entries.command: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File | Sort-Object Length -Descending | Select-Object -First 20 FullName, Length
entries.explain: Sorts every file by size and keeps the first 20.

actionTemplate.command: Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath {dir} -Recurse -File | Sort-Object Length -Descending | Select-Object -First 20 FullName, Length

entries.title: Show the size of each folder
entries.command: Get-ChildItem -Directory | ForEach-Object { $s = (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object Length -Sum).Sum; [pscustomobject]@{ Folder = $_.Name; MB = [math]::Round($s / 1MB, 2) } } | Sort-Object MB -Descending
entries.explain: Adds up every file inside each subfolder. It reads everything, so big folders take time.

entries.title: Find files changed today
entries.explain: Compares each modified time with midnight today.

entries.title: Show the 10 newest files
entries.command: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 FullName, LastWriteTime
entries.explain: Sorts by last modified time, newest first.

entries.title: Find files older than 30 days
entries.explain: Handy before cleaning up. Review the list before deleting anything.

entries.title: Count files
entries.explain: The parentheses run the command first, then .Count counts the result.

entries.title: Count files by extension
entries.command: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File | Group-Object Extension | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object Name, Count
entries.explain: Groups files by extension and counts each group.

entries.title: Show the content of a text file
entries.explain: Prints the file. Pipe to Select-Object -First 20 for a preview.

entries.title: Show the first lines of a file
entries.explain: -TotalCount stops reading after that many lines, so it is quick on big files.

entries.title: Show the last lines of a file
entries.explain: Reads the end of the file.

entries.title: Watch a log file grow
entries.explain: Shows new lines as they are written. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

entries.title: Copy a file or folder
entries.explain: Add -Recurse to copy a folder with its content.

params.name: -Recurse
params.text: Copy a folder and everything inside

entries.title: Move or rename a file
entries.explain: Moving inside the same folder renames the file.

entries.title: Rename a file
entries.explain: The second value is just the new name, not a path.

entries.title: Create an empty file
entries.explain: Creates the file, and fails if it already exists unless you add -Force.

entries.title: Create a folder
entries.explain: Creates the folder and any missing parent folders. It fails if the folder already exists.

entries.title: Delete a file
entries.explain: Deletes permanently, it does not use the Recycle Bin. Add -WhatIf first to preview.

params.name: -WhatIf
params.text: Show what would happen without doing it

entries.title: Delete a folder and its content
entries.explain: Removes the folder and everything inside. There is no undo.

entries.title: Find empty folders
entries.explain: Lists folders that contain nothing at all.

entries.title: Make a file read-only
entries.explain: Set the value to $false to make it writable again.

entries.title: Change a file's modified date
entries.explain: Also CreationTime and LastAccessTime.

entries.title: Hide or show a file
entries.explain: Use -= to remove the Hidden attribute again.

entries.title: Get the size of one file
entries.explain: The size is in bytes. Divide by 1KB or 1MB for readable numbers.

entries.title: Copy only the folder structure
entries.explain: Recreates every subfolder without the files.

entries.title: Create a symbolic link
entries.explain: Needs Developer Mode or administrator rights. Use -ItemType Junction for folders without that need.

entries.title: Find text inside files
entries.explain: Shows the file, line number and line for each match.

params.name: -Pattern
params.text: Text or regular expression to find

params.name: -SimpleMatch
params.text: Treat the pattern as plain text

params.name: -CaseSensitive
params.text: Match upper and lower case exactly

params.name: -Context 2
params.text: Also show 2 lines around each match

entries.example: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File | Select-String -Pattern 'hello' | Select-Object Path, LineNumber, Line

actionTemplate.command: Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath {dir} -Recurse -File | Select-String -Pattern {input:Text to find} | Select-Object Path, LineNumber, Line

entries.title: List only the files that contain a word
entries.explain: -List stops at the first match per file.

entries.title: Search with exact capitalisation
entries.explain: Select-String ignores case by default.

entries.title: Search with a regular expression
entries.explain: Patterns follow .NET regular expression rules.

entries.title: Count matching lines
entries.explain: Counts the lines that matched.

entries.title: Show lines that do not match
entries.explain: -NotMatch inverts the search.

entries.title: Find files by name
entries.explain: Wildcards * and ? work in -Filter.

entries.title: Find files whose name matches a pattern
entries.explain: -match uses regular expressions, -like uses wildcards.

entries.title: Find files bigger than 1 MB
entries.explain: PowerShell understands KB, MB and GB as numbers.

entries.title: Search but skip some folders
entries.explain: Filters out files whose path contains the unwanted folder names.

entries.title: Find the first match and stop
entries.explain: Select-Object -First stops the pipeline early.

entries.title: Find where a command lives
entries.explain: Shows the program that runs when you type the name.

entries.title: Find duplicate files by content
entries.command: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File | Get-FileHash | Group-Object Hash | Where-Object Count -gt 1 | ForEach-Object { $_.Group.Path }
entries.explain: Two files with the same hash have the same content.

entries.title: Replace text in many files
entries.explain: Reads each file, replaces the text and writes it back. Try on a copy first.

entries.title: Change file extensions in bulk
entries.explain: Renames every matching file. Add -WhatIf to preview.

entries.title: Count lines of code by extension
entries.command: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File -Include *.py,*.js,*.cs | Group-Object Extension | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ Ext = $_.Name; Files = $_.Count; Lines = ($_.Group | Get-Content | Measure-Object -Line).Lines } }
entries.explain: Totals lines for each file type.

entries.title: Keep only some columns
entries.explain: Select-Object chooses which properties to show.

entries.title: Filter rows
entries.explain: Keeps only the objects for which the test is true. Inside the braces $_ is the current object.

entries.title: Filter rows with the short form
entries.explain: The short form works for one simple test.

entries.title: Sort the results
entries.explain: Add -Descending to reverse the order.

entries.title: Take the first or last items
entries.explain: Use -Last for the end and -Skip to skip items.

entries.title: Remove duplicates
entries.explain: Sort-Object -Unique, or Select-Object -Unique on an already sorted list.

entries.title: Count how often each value appears
entries.explain: Group-Object counts identical values.

entries.title: Add up, average, min and max
entries.explain: Calculates statistics over a numeric property.

entries.title: Run something for every item
entries.explain: The braces run once per item. The alias % is the short name.

entries.title: See which properties an object has
entries.explain: Shows the names and types of properties and methods, which tells you what you can select.

entries.title: Get plain values instead of objects
entries.explain: -ExpandProperty returns just the values so that text tools can use them.

entries.title: Add a calculated column
entries.explain: A hashtable with Name and Expression creates a new column.

entries.title: Group items
entries.explain: Collects items that share a value.

entries.title: Show output and save it too
entries.explain: Writes to the file and passes the objects on.

entries.title: Compare two lists
entries.explain: => means only in the second list, <= only in the first.

entries.title: Join items into one line
entries.explain: -join glues the items together with a separator.

entries.title: Split text into lines
entries.explain: -split cuts a string at the separator and returns an array.

entries.title: Get one value out of an object
entries.explain: Parentheses followed by .Property reads a single property.

entries.title: Run in parallel (PowerShell 7)
entries.explain: Runs the block on several threads at once. Variables from outside need the $using: prefix.

entries.title: Pass many parameters as a hashtable
entries.explain: Splatting keeps long commands readable. Use @ instead of $ when passing it.

entries.title: Do something only if a condition is true
entries.explain: The classic if/else.

entries.title: Handle errors
entries.explain: -ErrorAction Stop turns an error into one that catch can handle.

entries.title: Show results as a table
entries.explain: Format-Table is for display only. Do not pipe its output into other commands.

entries.title: Show every property of an item
entries.explain: Shows all properties as name and value pairs.

entries.title: Show names in several columns
entries.explain: Compact multi-column listing.

entries.title: Show results in a searchable window
entries.explain: A sortable, filterable window. It is not available in PowerShell 7 without the GraphicalTools module.

entries.title: Save results as CSV
entries.explain: Creates a CSV file that opens in Excel.

entries.title: Read a CSV file
entries.explain: Each row becomes an object with the column names as properties.

entries.title: Filter a CSV and save the result
entries.explain: Reads, filters, writes.

entries.title: Read JSON text
entries.explain: Turns JSON text into objects.

entries.title: Turn objects into JSON
entries.explain: -Depth 5 keeps nested objects. The default depth is only 2.

entries.title: Read a JSON file
entries.explain: -Raw reads the whole file as one string, which JSON needs.

entries.title: Make an HTML report
entries.command: Get-Process | Select-Object -First 5 Name, Id | ConvertTo-Html | Set-Content $env:TEMP\report.html
entries.explain: Creates a simple table as a web page.

entries.title: Save text to a file
entries.explain: Same as the > operator. Use -Encoding utf8 for a specific encoding.

entries.title: Add a line to a file
entries.explain: Appends instead of replacing.

entries.title: Read an XML file
entries.explain: Gives you an object you can navigate with dots.

entries.title: Turn objects into text
entries.explain: Useful when a command needs a plain string.

entries.title: Output only the values
entries.explain: Without column headers or decoration.

entries.title: Print in colour
entries.explain: Write-Host writes to the screen only, not into the pipeline.

entries.title: Stop output being cut off
entries.explain: -AutoSize sizes the columns to fit, -Wrap wraps long values.

entries.title: Read the clipboard
entries.explain: Returns whatever text is on the clipboard.

entries.title: Put text on the clipboard
entries.explain: Anything piped in is copied.

entries.title: Copy a command's output
entries.explain: Great for pasting a file list into a chat or email.

entries.title: Copy a file's text
entries.explain: -Raw keeps line breaks as they are.

entries.title: Copy a file's full path
entries.explain: Handy when you need the path in another program.

entries.title: Add to what is on the clipboard
entries.explain: Reads the clipboard, adds text and puts it back.

entries.title: Read the clipboard as lines
entries.explain: Without -Raw you get one item per line.

entries.title: Sort the lines on the clipboard
entries.explain: Replaces the clipboard with the sorted lines.

entries.title: Remove duplicate lines on the clipboard
entries.explain: Keeps one copy of each line.

entries.title: Change clipboard text to upper case
entries.explain: Also ToLower() and Trim().

entries.title: Copy files so they can be pasted in Explorer
entries.explain: Puts the file itself on the clipboard, not its text.

entries.title: Clear the clipboard
entries.explain: Removes the text from the clipboard.

entries.title: Get the size of an image on the clipboard
entries.explain: Returns nothing when the clipboard has no image.

entries.title: Where is the clipboard history?
entries.explain: Windows has its own clipboard history. Press Win+V to use it.

entries.title: List running programs
entries.explain: Shows every process with memory and CPU use.

entries.title: Find the programs using the most memory
entries.command: Get-Process | Sort-Object WorkingSet64 -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 Name, Id, @{n='MB';e={[math]::Round($_.WorkingSet64 / 1MB)}}
entries.explain: Sorts by memory in use.

entries.title: Find the programs using the most CPU time
entries.command: Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 Name, Id, CPU
entries.explain: CPU is total processor seconds since the program started.

entries.title: Find a program by name
entries.explain: Add * for a partial match, for example chr*.

entries.title: Stop a program by name
entries.explain: Closes every process with that name immediately. Unsaved work is lost.

entries.title: Stop a program by process ID
entries.explain: Find the ID with Get-Process.

entries.title: Start a program
entries.explain: Starts and returns immediately. Add -Wait to wait until it ends.

params.name: -Wait
params.text: Wait for the program to finish

entries.title: Start a program as administrator
entries.explain: Triggers the Windows prompt for administrator rights.

entries.title: Wait for a program to close
entries.explain: Blocks until the process ends.

entries.title: Find which program uses a port
entries.explain: Replace 3000 with the port. Nothing is returned when the port is free.

entries.title: Show the full command line of a program
entries.explain: Shows the arguments each program was started with.

entries.title: Time how long a command takes
entries.explain: Returns a TimeSpan. Output of the command itself is hidden.

entries.title: Show which user runs each program
entries.explain: Needs administrator rights to see other users' processes.

entries.title: Change a program's priority
entries.explain: Lower priority gives other programs more CPU time.

entries.title: List files a program has loaded
entries.explain: $PID is the ID of the current PowerShell session.

entries.title: Run a command in the background
entries.explain: Receive-Job returns the output. Get-Job lists the jobs.

entries.title: List services
entries.explain: Shows each service with its status.

entries.title: List only running services
entries.explain: Filters on the Status property.

entries.title: Find automatic services that are stopped
entries.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where-Object { $_.StartMode -eq 'Auto' -and $_.State -ne 'Running' } | Select-Object Name, State
entries.explain: Often a sign that something failed at startup.

entries.title: Find a service by name
entries.explain: The name can be the short name or use wildcards.

entries.title: Show details of a service
entries.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -Filter "Name = 'Spooler'" | Format-List Name, State, StartMode, PathName, StartName
entries.explain: Shows the program, startup type and account.

entries.title: Start a service
entries.explain: Needs administrator rights.

entries.title: Stop a service
entries.explain: Needs administrator rights. Dependent services stop too, add -Force.

entries.title: Restart a service
entries.explain: Needs administrator rights.

entries.title: Change how a service starts
entries.explain: Automatic, Manual or Disabled. Needs administrator rights.

entries.title: Show what a service depends on
entries.explain: Use DependentServices for the other direction.

entries.title: Count services by status
entries.command: Get-Service | Group-Object Status | Select-Object Name, Count
entries.explain: A quick health overview.

entries.title: Wait until a service is running
entries.explain: Throws when the service does not reach that status in time.

entries.title: Show my IP addresses
entries.explain: Lists the local IPv4 address of each adapter.

entries.title: Show my public IP address
entries.explain: Asks a website, so it needs internet access.

entries.title: List network adapters
entries.command: Get-NetAdapter | Select-Object Name, Status, LinkSpeed, MacAddress
entries.explain: Shows wired and wireless adapters.

entries.title: Check whether a computer answers
entries.explain: Like ping. Needs internet for external names.

entries.title: Test whether a TCP port is open
entries.explain: TcpTestSucceeded tells you if the connection worked.

entries.title: Look up a DNS name
entries.explain: Shows the IP addresses and record types.

entries.title: Clear the DNS cache
entries.explain: Fixes stale name lookups. Run as administrator.

entries.title: Show which ports are listening
entries.command: Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess | Sort-Object LocalPort
entries.explain: Lists the programs that accept connections.

entries.title: Show active connections
entries.command: Get-NetTCPConnection -State Established | Select-Object -First 20 RemoteAddress, RemotePort, OwningProcess
entries.explain: Established connections to other computers.

entries.title: Download a file
entries.explain: Saves the response to a file.

entries.title: Call a JSON web service
entries.explain: Returns the JSON already converted to objects.

entries.title: Send JSON to a web service
entries.explain: Sends a POST request with a JSON body.

entries.title: List saved Wi-Fi networks
entries.explain: Shows the networks this PC has joined.

entries.title: Show a saved Wi-Fi password
entries.command: netsh wlan show profile name="MyWifi" key=clear
entries.explain: Look for Key Content in the output. Needs administrator rights to show the key.

entries.title: Show the routing table
entries.explain: Where network traffic goes.

entries.title: Show the hosts file
entries.explain: Maps names to addresses before DNS is asked.

entries.title: List shared folders
entries.explain: Shows the folders this PC shares on the network.

entries.title: Trace the route to a host
entries.explain: Shows each hop on the way.

entries.title: Show the Windows version
entries.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption, Version, OSArchitecture
entries.explain: Edition, build number and 32 or 64 bit.

entries.title: Show when the PC last started
entries.explain: The last boot time. Fast startup can make this older than expected.

entries.title: Show how long the PC has been running
entries.explain: Returns a time span.

entries.title: Show the processor
entries.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object Name, NumberOfCores, NumberOfLogicalProcessors
entries.explain: Model, cores and threads.

entries.title: Show installed memory
entries.explain: Total physical RAM.

entries.title: Show free memory
entries.explain: Memory that is currently unused.

entries.title: Show BIOS and serial number
entries.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_BIOS | Select-Object Manufacturer, SMBIOSBIOSVersion, SerialNumber
entries.explain: Useful for support calls.

entries.title: Show the computer model
entries.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem | Select-Object Manufacturer, Model, Name
entries.explain: Maker, model and computer name.

entries.title: Show the graphics card
entries.explain: Name and driver of each graphics adapter.

entries.title: Create a battery report
entries.explain: Creates an HTML report with capacity and usage history.

entries.title: List installed Windows updates
entries.explain: Shows recent updates. It can take a few seconds.

entries.title: Show everything about this PC
entries.explain: The classic summary of hardware, network and updates. It takes a few seconds.

entries.title: Show the current user and computer
entries.explain: Environment variables hold the names.

entries.title: Show the PowerShell version
entries.explain: Version, edition and platform.

entries.title: Show connected monitors
entries.command: Get-CimInstance WmiMonitorID -Namespace root\wmi | ForEach-Object { ($_.UserFriendlyName | Where-Object { $_ -ne 0 } | ForEach-Object { [char]$_ }) -join '' }
entries.explain: Reads the monitor names. Laptops with one screen show one name.

entries.title: Show free space on each drive
entries.explain: Used and free space per drive letter.

entries.title: List volumes
entries.explain: Label, file system, size and health.

entries.title: List physical disks
entries.command: Get-PhysicalDisk | Select-Object FriendlyName, MediaType, Size, HealthStatus
entries.explain: Shows SSD or HDD and health.

entries.title: List partitions
entries.command: Get-Partition | Select-Object DiskNumber, PartitionNumber, DriveLetter, Size
entries.explain: Shows how each disk is divided.

entries.title: Get the size of one folder
entries.explain: The result is in MB.

entries.title: See how big the temp folder is
entries.explain: Temporary files you can usually remove.

entries.title: Delete old temporary files
entries.command: Get-ChildItem $env:TEMP -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object LastWriteTime -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-7) | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
entries.explain: Removes temp files older than a week. Files in use are skipped.

entries.title: Empty the Recycle Bin
entries.explain: Permanently removes what is in the bin.

entries.title: Check a drive for errors
entries.explain: Scans without changing anything. Needs administrator rights.

entries.title: Check disk health
entries.command: Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter | Select-Object DeviceId, Temperature, Wear, ReadErrorsTotal
entries.explain: Predictive health data, when the disk reports it. Needs administrator rights.

entries.title: Mount an ISO file
entries.explain: Opens it as a virtual drive. Use Dismount-DiskImage to remove it.

entries.title: List removable drives
entries.explain: USB sticks and card readers.

entries.title: Map a network folder to a drive letter
entries.explain: The drive stays after you close PowerShell.

entries.title: Show the biggest folders in your profile
entries.command: Get-ChildItem $env:USERPROFILE -Directory | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $_.Name; GB = [math]::Round(((Get-ChildItem $_.FullName -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object Length -Sum).Sum / 1GB), 2) } } | Sort-Object GB -Descending
entries.explain: Finds out where your space went. It can take a minute.

entries.title: Read a registry value
entries.explain: Shows the value and its name.

entries.title: List the keys below a key
entries.explain: Registry keys work like folders.

entries.title: Write a registry value
entries.explain: Writes to the current user's part of the registry. Make a backup first.

entries.title: Create a registry key
entries.explain: Creates the key. It fails if the key already exists.

entries.title: Delete a registry value
entries.explain: Removes only that value.

entries.title: Delete a registry key
entries.explain: Removes the key and everything below it. Export it first.

entries.title: Back up a registry key
entries.explain: Creates a .reg file you can double-click to restore.

entries.title: Restore a registry file
entries.explain: Writes the keys from a .reg file back.

entries.title: Search the registry for text
entries.explain: Slow on big hives, so start in a narrow key.

entries.title: Check whether a key exists
entries.explain: Returns True or False.

entries.title: Read machine-wide settings
entries.command: Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion' | Select-Object ProductName, DisplayVersion, CurrentBuild
entries.explain: HKLM is for the whole computer, HKCU for the current user.

entries.title: List programs that start with Windows
entries.explain: The Run key holds the user's startup entries.

entries.title: List registry drives
entries.explain: HKCU: and HKLM: behave like drive letters.

entries.title: List environment variables
entries.explain: Shows every variable and its value.

entries.title: Read one environment variable
entries.explain: Use $env: followed by the name.

entries.title: Set a variable for this window only
entries.explain: Disappears when you close PowerShell.

entries.title: Set a variable permanently for your account
entries.explain: New windows will see it. Existing ones need a restart.

entries.title: Remove a permanent variable
entries.explain: Setting it to null deletes it.

entries.title: Show the folders in PATH
entries.explain: One folder per line.

entries.title: Show the PATH that belongs to your account
entries.explain: User PATH is added to the machine PATH.

entries.title: Show the machine-wide PATH
entries.explain: Changing it needs administrator rights.

entries.title: Add a folder to your PATH
entries.explain: Only for you, permanent. Open a new window to use it.

entries.title: Check that every PATH folder exists
entries.explain: Lists broken entries.

entries.title: Find duplicate PATH entries
entries.command: $env:Path -split ';' | Group-Object | Where-Object Count -gt 1 | Select-Object Name, Count
entries.explain: Duplicates slow nothing down but make the list messy.

entries.title: Reload PATH in this window
entries.explain: Useful after an installer changed PATH.

entries.title: Find the temp folder
entries.explain: Where programs keep temporary files.

entries.title: Show where modules are searched
entries.explain: The folders PowerShell scans for modules.

entries.title: List scheduled tasks
entries.command: Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object State -ne Disabled | Select-Object -First 20 TaskName, State
entries.explain: Shows the jobs Windows runs on a schedule.

entries.title: Show when a task last ran
entries.command: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTaskMachineCore*' | Get-ScheduledTaskInfo | Select-Object TaskName, LastRunTime, LastTaskResult, NextRunTime
entries.explain: LastTaskResult 0 means success.

entries.title: Run a script every day
entries.explain: Creates the task for your account.

entries.title: Run a script at logon
entries.explain: Starts each time you sign in.

entries.title: Run a task now
entries.explain: Starts it immediately, without waiting for the schedule.

entries.title: Disable a task
entries.explain: Keeps the task but stops it from running.

entries.title: Enable a task
entries.explain: Turns a disabled task back on.

entries.title: Delete a task
entries.explain: Removes the task for good.

entries.title: Export a task to XML
entries.explain: Use it as a backup or to copy the task to another PC.

entries.title: Find tasks that failed last time
entries.command: Get-ScheduledTask | Get-ScheduledTaskInfo | Where-Object { $_.LastTaskResult -ne 0 -and $_.LastRunTime.Year -gt 2000 } | Select-Object TaskName, LastRunTime, LastTaskResult
